identity.title: Train for the Worst, Plan for the Best: Understanding Token Ordering in Masked Diffusions

problem.claim: The work examines the tradeoff between masked diffusion models’ difficult training subproblems and their flexible inference-time token ordering.

contributions.claim: Analyzes the computational difficulty of the infilling subproblems MDMs face during training relative to autoregressive models.
Introduces adaptive token-order selection at inference to help MDMs avoid hard subproblems.
Shows that adaptive decoding can substantially improve pretrained MDM performance on logic puzzles.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors frame MDM behavior through a joint examination of training-time computational difficulty and inference-time decoding-order flexibility.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report theoretical and empirical evidence that MDMs train on computationally intractable subproblems compared with autoregressive counterparts.
The authors report that adaptive token ordering significantly enhances MDM capabilities by sidestepping hard subproblems.

On Sudoku, the authors report that adaptive inference raises pretrained MDM solving accuracy from below 7% to approximately 90%, exceeding autoregressive models explicitly teacher-forced to learn the decoding order.

narrative_sequence.summary: MDMs exchange greater training complexity for flexible inference-time token ordering compared with autoregressive models.
The work examines the two sides of this tradeoff and reports that MDM training contains computationally intractable subproblems.
Adaptive inference selects token orders to bypass difficult subproblems, with a reported Sudoku improvement from below 7% to about 90%.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links an identified training bottleneck to an inference strategy that changes token ordering, then reports a task-specific performance comparison.

lessons.interpretation: A paper can make a stronger mechanistic case when its intervention directly targets the stated source of difficulty.
lessons.application: When presenting a difficult training or computation problem, connect the proposed inference or algorithmic choice explicitly to that bottleneck and evaluate the matched mechanism on a concrete task.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the intervention does not address the proposed bottleneck or when the task has no meaningful ordering or adaptive-decision structure.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the theoretical assumptions, empirical setup, model sizes, datasets beyond Sudoku, or statistical uncertainty.
It does not explain the adaptive decoding rule or establish whether the reported gains generalize beyond the stated logic-puzzle setting.
